narrative.overview:
A dark kitchen at night with exactly one heat source. The whole product sits on warm near-black charcoal, and a single burnt-orange ember is the only saturated thing most screens contain. Where the ember appears — a tab, a total, a save button armed with unsaved changes, a Glovo reminder, a day that beat its target — it means this is the live, actionable number. Everywhere else the interface is quiet: bone-coloured text, hairline borders, four steps of charcoal, and generous rounding.

The mood is warm industrial and low-light, because the primary usage scene is a phone held at a truck after service, sometimes in the dark, and the secondary is a desktop admin session at the end of the day. Heat is information, not decoration: the accent is never used to make something pretty, only to report state, rank or urgency. Density follows the surface: the generator (index.html) is one column of big touch targets, the admin (admin.html) is a dense grid of tables, tiles and week cards that still resolves to a single readable column on a phone.

Everything is tactile and confident: controls are chunky (44px minimum, pills for anything selectable), pressed states are immediate, and hover performs no lift-shift — the system settles rather than floats. Depth is tonal, not cast: surfaces separate by four charcoal steps and hairline borders, and the only glow in the system is a state glow on the one thing that is currently live or successful. The product is Polish, terse and unpretentious; the interface never explains itself twice.
keyCharacteristics: Four-step warm charcoal shell with hairline separation and no ambient shadow at rest.
One ember accent, reserved for live state, primaries and success — not for decoration.
System font stack, hierarchy from size and weight; money, hours and quantities are always tabular.
Pills for anything the user selects; 6px and 12px radii for containers and fields.
44px touch targets and safe-area-aware fixed actions on the phone surface; density only in the admin.
Material Symbols Rounded, inline and decorative, one icon language on both surfaces.

rules.name: The One Ember Rule
rules.body: Grill Orange and its washes cover roughly a tenth of any screen or less. It marks live state, the primary action, rank and success-adjacent emphasis — never a decorative background, never two competing ember elements in one card. Its rarity is what makes it read as heat.

rules.name: The No New Hex Rule
rules.body: New tints are made with color-mix() from a palette value and an existing surface — never a new literal colour outside this file. Every tint in the system is a percentage of Grill Orange, a semantic colour, or a charcoal step.

rules.name: The Glovo Gold Is Warning Rule
rules.body: Gold means delivery or "watch this", and the two never need to be told apart because both mean attention. It is never a general-purpose highlight; that job belongs to the ember.

rules.name: The Ember Text Rule
rules.body: Grill Orange is a state colour, not a text colour and not a fill. As text on charcoal it measures 3.45-4.43:1, so it is only legible enough at 24px and above, where the large-text threshold applies; at body and label sizes the ember step for text is Grill Orange Hover (4.86-5.74:1). As a fill behind text, use Grill Orange Fill (5.74:1 with inverse text) - Grill Orange itself is never the background of a control that carries a label, because inverse text on it reaches only 4.43:1.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Any value a person might compare down a column — money, hours, quantities, percentages, dates in tables — carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Set it wherever a number is rendered, not on the table as a whole.

rules.name: The Two-Size Label Rule
rules.body: Labels are either 12px (field and kicker labels, --text-muted or --text-secondary) or 14px (everything readable). Nothing in the interface renders below 12px except inside chips and badges, where 12px is the floor.

rules.name: The No Second Family Rule
rules.body: No webfont, no mono face, no display face. The only downloaded font is the icon font; adding a text font costs a request on a phone at a truck.

rules.name: The Closed Scale Rule
rules.body: Four sizes (24 / 18 / 14 / 12) and two weights (400 / 700) are the entire type scale. There is no fifth size and no 500/600 weight; overflow is solved with wrapping, truncation or layout, never with a new size or a thinner weight.

rules.name: The 40px Rule
rules.body: No interactive target measures under 40x40px. The generator's tabs, quantity steppers and header links sit at 40-46px, its fields and selects at 44-45px, and the FAB and sheet rows at 56px; the admin's compressed week tabs, pagination and chart selects stop at 36px. Icon actions keep a 44px hit area even when the glyph is 20px.

rules.name: The One Action Bar Rule
rules.body: The generator has exactly one persistent action area, the fixed bottom bar. New actions go into a card or the bottom sheet — never a second floating control.

rules.name: The Safe-Area Rule
rules.body: Anything fixed to a viewport edge pads with the matching env(safe-area-inset-*): the generator's bottom bar and sheet, the admin toast layer at the top.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces do not lift on hover and do not cast ambient shadows. If something needs attention, change its border colour, its background step, or give it an ember glow — do not add a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Glow Means State Rule
rules.body: A glow is never styling. It appears only on the primary or active control, a success state, or an overlay that must detach from the page.

rules.name: The No Cast Light Rule
rules.body: No gradients, no backdrop blur, no stacked shadow effects, no skeuomorphic surfaces. Depth is tone and hairline; the only filter in the system is the drop-shadow glow on the attention icon, which is a state, not a material.

rules.name: The Pill Means Selectable Rule
rules.body: A pill shape means the user picks it: tabs, filters, week selectors, counters, badges. Outlined rectangles mean fields, actions and containers — never selection.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Provisional Rule
rules.body: Dashed borders indicate absence, invitation or archive — never a normal state.

dos: Do pull every colour through the tokens in css/theme/palette.css; tint with color-mix() against a surface token (e.g. color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary-color) 14%, var(--surface-raised))).
Do use Grill Orange Hover for orange text at body and label sizes, and Grill Orange Fill as the background of every filled ember control so inverse text clears AA.
Do reserve Grill Orange for live state, primary action, selection and success-adjacent emphasis, at roughly a tenth of the screen or less.
Do keep targets at 40px or larger - 44px for inputs and primary actions, 36px for the admin's compressed controls - and pad fixed edges with env(safe-area-inset-*).
Do render every comparable number with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, and give each value its state through colour plus one hairline, not a filled block.
Do use pills for anything selectable, 6px for fields and actions, 12px for containers, and dashed borders only for add/empty/archived.
Do keep depth tonal and flat: change border tone, background step or add an ember/success glow.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion: reduce for every transition, glow, confetti and loader animation.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces from the palette - scrollbars, text selection (::selection) and focus rings all carry design, and the caret already inherits the text colour.

Do gate feedback through noticeService / dialogService with the semantic --info/--success/--danger/--warning/--muted/--loading treatments, and keep icons aria-hidden with real Material Symbols ligature names.
donts: Don't introduce a hex, rgb() or hsl() literal outside css/theme/palette.css.
Don't add a text webfont, a second family or a mono face; the system stack plus Material Symbols is the whole type budget.
Don't lift surfaces on hover, add ambient shadows to cards, or animate transform on buttons and rows — the overrides deliberately strip these.
Don't use Glovo Gold as a general highlight, or Lettuce Green / Tomato Red for anything other than success/money and destructive/negative.
Don't put cards inside cards; repeated content inside a card is a tile, a row or a list item.
Don't use native alert/confirm/prompt, or native select/date/time popups — the custom control layer owns those interactions.
Don't render a value below 12px, or set a label in body weight; labels are 12px/700 with 0.02em tracking.
Don't reach for a fifth type size, a third weight, a gradient, a backdrop blur or a stacked shadow to solve a density or emphasis problem.
Don't add a second floating action on the generator or hide the fixed action bar to make room for content.
